subject: cap rate vs cash-on-cash
preheader: one screens the asset. the other includes your financing and cash invested.
headline: Cap rate excludes financing. Cash-on-cash includes it.
body: Cap rate excludes financing and compares modeled net operating income with property value. It can help compare properties on a common basis, but it does not predict what you will pocket.

Cash-on-cash return is modeled annual pre-tax cash flow divided by total cash invested. For illustration, $7,000 of modeled annual cash flow on $70,000 invested is 10%. Verify which cash outlays and recurring costs apply to your property.

Financing can make cash-on-cash return differ sharply from cap rate because debt service and cash invested change the calculation. The direction and size of that difference depend on the inputs; neither metric is an investment verdict.
Use cap rate, cash-on-cash return, and DSCR as separate screening views, then validate the rent, expenses, financing, and cash-required assumptions behind them.
For a supported address, TrueCap asks for the asking price and shows editable assumptions before calculating these metrics. The preliminary screen is free and does not require a card.
